messages:
Nora (Finance): Quick company-wide notice: updated expense & consultant/vendor approval policy goes live Mon Jun 14. Short summary below and full doc on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/finance/expense-consultant-policy :loudspeaker:

Chris (Travel Ops): TL;DR travel/per diem and team-card limits:
```
- Team virtual-card single charge cap: $3,000 (requests above require finance approval)
- Per diem: $75/day domestic, $120/day international (meals + incidentals)
- Hotel guideline: midscale business hotels; exceptions allowed with manager + Ops approval
```

Mei (Eng): For contractors/consultants: any vendor-supplied consulting > $5k must have a statement of work (SOW) and PO. Does this apply to 1099 contractors paid via card?

Nora (Finance): Yes. Thresholds are based on total engagement amount. Single card charges for contractors under $1,500 still allowed but cumulative spend across the engagement must be tracked and may trigger a PO/SOW requirement. If in doubt, open a procurement ticket and tag @Jordan.

Jordan (Vendor Ops): New flow for consultant onboarding: submit Vendor Intake + SOW + W-9 (or W-8) in the ticket. If the consultant will access prod data, include security attestation from Security team. We'll fast-track known vendors but still need docs.

compliance-bot: Reminder: all expense reports for managers approving contractor spend must include supporting receipts and the project code. Missing receipts may cause chargebacks to the approving manager. (Policy ref: EXP-2026-06)

Mei (Eng): How should teams track cumulative contractor spend? We often hire contractors monthly at ~$1k per month, could exceed $5k over time.

Nora (Finance): Use the Procurement ticket to create an engagement entry and tag FP&A. Procurement will set an engagement ID and monitor cumulative spend. We recommend setting a 6-month review for recurring contractor arrangements.

Chris (Travel Ops): A couple process notes: 1) All travel bookings should go through our travel portal to ensure policy rates and insurer coverage. 2) If you need an exception for a higher-rate hotel for safety reasons, include justification in the ticket.

Jordan (Vendor Ops): Invoice processing change: please submit invoices via Bill.com with the Procurement ticket number in the subject. Invoices submitted outside Bill.com will be returned. This reduces PO/invoice mismatches.

Nora (Finance): Action items:
- Managers: review team card holders and revoke unused cards by June 21.
- Teams with contractors approaching $5k total spend: open a procurement ticket to create engagement and SOW.
- Anyone who approves contractor expenses: complete the 10-min compliance micro-training (link on Confluence).

Mei (Eng): A couple edge cases: open-source contractors paid in multiple currencies, and reimbursements for test lab supplies. Any guidance?

Nora (Finance): For multi-currency payments, Procurement will handle FX and may require bank details. Test lab supplies reimbursed to employees still follow the $75/day per diem guideline for meals; supplies should be expensed with receipts and project code. If supply spend is recurring, consider converting to vendor purchase.

compliance-bot: New audit schedule: random vendor/contractor audits will run quarterly. Teams flagged for irregularities will get a follow-up.

Jordan (Vendor Ops): If you need an exception to any of the above, open a ticket with subject "PROCURE-EXCEPTION" and include justification, duration, and manager signoff. We aim to respond within 3 business days.

Nora (Finance): Thanks all. We'll post the recorded Q&A and an FAQ on Confluence later today. If you want a tailored walkthrough for your org, reply here with 2 preferred times. :white_check_mark:
